script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: The text says Haman was elevated above the princes, not that he was a prince himself.
Mordecai is described as sitting and then standing at the gate. Esther 3:2 does not give his posture.
Saying Mordecai stays upright adds a posture the verse does not give.
The text does not say the servants passed Mordecai's identity as a Jew to Haman.
The text does not say the servants carried Mordecai's identity as a Jew to Haman.
The text does not say the servants reported Mordecai's identity as a Jew to Haman.
The text does not establish whether any of the gate servants were among the Jews targeted.
The text says the lot fell on a month; it does not say which day the lot picked.
The text says the lot fell on a month; it does not say which day the lot picked.
The passage calls Adar the twelfth month but does not say it is the last month of the year.
Haman gives the king more than the phrase 'a certain people.' The explanation also guesses why Haman left out the name, which the text does not say.
Saying Haman is making his pitch sound reasonable assigns him a motive the text does not give.
The comparison of bronze's value with silver's is not established by the passage.
The passage shows the ring sealing this order, not that it seals the king's orders generally.
The text does not say the king was wearing a crown or that it stayed on.
The passage does not establish that one language could not reach everybody or that the scribes had a long day ahead.
The text says the language of every people, not that each province had a single language of its own.
Being written in the king's name does not establish that Haman's name appeared nowhere on the order.
Saying the line was meant to be heavy assigns an intent the text does not state.
The text says the king and Haman sat down to drink, not that they stayed put while the letters traveled.
The text does not establish that nobody went to visit anybody.
The passage does not say the edict caused the city's confusion; the explanation makes that connection.
The text does not describe the king and Haman's drink as quiet.
